topic: The Great Depression and New Deal

question.leadin: Answer the following about the political career of Franklin D. Roosevelt.
question.text: In 1932, FDR defeated this man to become president. This president's administration oversaw the beginning of the Great Depression, for which he was widely unpopular.
question.clue: Near the end of his term, he sent Douglas MacArthur to clear out the Bonus Army that was protesting for relief from the Great Depression.

swap.leadin: On "Black Sunday" during this period, so-called "black blizzards" swept through the plains states.
swap.text: "Okies" migrated west during what period of severe drought and agriculture damage in the 1930s?
swap.clue: This event saw numerous storms referred to as black blizzards.

question.leadin: In Schechter Poultry Corporation v. United States, known as the "sick chicken case," the Supreme Court unanimously decided that this law was unconstitutional.
question.text: Name this piece of legislation, signed in 1933, that established the National Recovery Administration, known for its Blue Eagle emblem, and the Public Works Administration, which survived the Supreme Court's ruling in Schechter.
question.clue: It set up an agency headed by General Hugh S. Johnson that, and it reduced maximum hours so that more people couple be employed, while its Section 7a was an important concession to labor unions.

swap.text: The Microsoft lawsuit claimed it abused this economic status of being the only seller in its market and destroying competition.
swap.clue: Lizzie Magie developed the predecessor to this product in the Georgist community of Arden, Delaware. Charles Darrow was long credited as the inventor of this consumer product.

question.text: In Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, the Supreme Court held that in giving President Roosevelt the power to create new Codes of Fair Competition, the NIRA violated this article of the Constitution, which gives sole legislative power to Congress.
question.clue: What Article of the Constitution describes the format and powers of Congress?

swap.leadin: Douglas MacArthur used army infantry to help the police disperse this group.
swap.text: Identify this group of army veterans which marched on Washington in 1932 to demand redemption of their service certificates from World War I.
swap.clue: Pelham Glassford twice reinstated Walter Waters as the leader of this group, which Gladwin Bland described as "an immense hobo jungle."

question.leadin: Wilhelm Loeser helped this man disguise himself by giving him plastic surgery and trying to obliterate his fingerprints with acid.
question.text: Name this Depression-era gangster and bank robber. He was infamously betrayed to federal agents by Ana Cumpanas, the "Woman in Red."
question.clue: A general of this first name earned the epithet "Athlete of Christ" for his brilliant "Long Campaign" against the Ottomans.

swap.leadin: The sixteenth of these described American industry as an "arsenal of democracy" for the world.
swap.text: Name this series of addresses with such titles as "On the Recession" and "Report on the Home Front."
swap.clue: Similar speeches were given while their speaker was Governor of New York.

question.leadin: This woman sent a letter to the New York Times complaining about being called "Mrs. Putnam" rather than her birth name.
question.text: Name this woman who celebrated other women pioneers in her field in her memoir The Fun of It. This woman died en route to Howland Island.
question.clue: In July 2017 National Geographic sent border collies to a Kiribati island to investigate this person, while the History Channel claimed she was captured by the Japanese.

swap.text: Al Capone was arrested for tax evasion after being investigated by this head of the Untouchables.
swap.clue: This man's inability to be bribed by the Chicago Outfit led him and his men to be labeled the "Untouchables."

question.leadin: This man was the Chairman of the State Factory Investigating Committee after the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire.
question.text: Name this New York Senator who is best known for being the namesake of the 1935 National Labor Relations Act, which created the National Labor Relations Board and guaranteed the right of workers to form unions.

swap.leadin: In his fanciful book My First Days in the White House, he discussed his potential Cabinet appointees.
swap.text: Name this governor who was gearing up for a 1936 presidential run when he was assassinated by Carl Weiss.
swap.clue: This ally of Father Charles Coughlin promoted socialist reforms in his Share the Wealth campaign which promised to make "every man a king."

question.leadin: Answer the following concerning the illustrious career of Brown graduate Charles Evan Hughes.
question.text: As Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, Hughes wrote the majority opinion in this 1935 case, which ruled that the National Industrial Recovery Act's regulations of a poultry corporation were unconstitutional.
question.answer: Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States
question.clue: This 1935 Supreme Court Case that ruled a certain piece of New Deal legislation had overreached itself because the namesake company did not engage in direct interstate commerce.

swap.leadin: A group of this many Black students in Rock Hill, South Carolina, pioneered the "Jail, No Bail" strategy after being arrested at a sit-in.
swap.text: What number also appears in the most common name of a 1972 anti-discrimination provision in education authored primarily by Patsy Mink?
swap.answerHtml: nine [accept Title IX; accept Friendship Nine or Rock Hill Nine]
swap.clue: Countee Cullen wrote about a group of this many people that ends "Surely, I said, / Now will the poets sing. / But they have raised no cry. / I wonder why."

question.leadin: The millionaire James Howe established a Madison Street college for these people where professors from the University of Chicago and Northwestern taught.
question.text: Name these people who popularized "mulligan stew" during the Great Depression.
question.clue: John Hodgman's The Areas of My Expertise includes matters pertaining to this group right after cryptozoology in its subtitle and provides a list of 700 names of people bearing this designation.

swap.text: In a speech, Perkins described this man responding only "Okay" to her proposal of unemployment insurance. Perkins and this head of the PWA were the only cabinet members to remain in office for FDR's entire presidency.
swap.answerHtml: Harold L. Ickes (“ICK-iss”) [do not accept or prompt on “Harold M. Ickes”]
swap.clue: One person with this last name chaired Bill Clinton's 1992 presidential campaign and was nicknamed the "Garbage Man" by (+) Michael Lewis in an unflattering 1997 profile.

question.leadin: While its first chairman was Peter Norbeck, this group was named for its fourth chief counsel, who would later become a commissioner of the SEC.
question.text: Name this commission which was established to explore the causes of the Wall Street Crash of 1929.
question.clue: Among the sections in the 400-page report produced by this investigative body were ones on "Manipulative devices," and "Abuse of proxies," as well as a chapter dedicated to investigating "Income-tax Avoidances."

swap.leadin: Identify the following about a New Deal agency FTPE.
swap.text: Called the "Father of the TVA," he is the namesake of the first TVA dam constructed. This Nebraska senator was later the co-author of an act that restricted the use of injunctions in labor disputes.
swap.clue: Profiles in Courage praises this "gentle knight" for leading the House "revolt" against Speaker Joseph Cannon.

question.text: The "Special Committee" that preceded HUAC investigated this supposed fascist-industrialist plan to overthrow FDR, which was revealed when the awesomely named Smedley Butler claimed that Gerald MacGuire tried to hire him to stage a coup d'etat.
question.answerHtml: the Business Plot [accept White House Putsch; prompt on Plot Against FDR or equivalents]
question.clue: Robert Clark employed one man involved in this incident, the only conspirator to testify before the McCormack-Dickstein committee.

swap.text: This man was the first director of the NRA and Time's Man of the Year in 1933. He called for a "blanket code" including a minimum wage, maximum workweek, and abolition of child labor, but was fired in 1934 after handing out leaflets praising Mussolini's "Corporate State."
